Recovery compares you with your own norm, so it needs a baseline first: at least 5 nights of HRV or resting heart rate with the ring worn. Sleep alone is not enough.
Indicative only, not a medical device.

Shares of the time asleep, against ranges typical of healthy adults of your age. The ring only estimates its stages and people differ a lot: a rough guide, not a finding.

If you feel unwell, call your doctor or the emergency number. Do not wait for the app.
Heart rate up or feeling off? Run a check: heart, HRV, SpO2 and your recent context.
Stress measurement is not available on this ring
Not set: calories, training load and fitness estimates stay off until you choose a sex and adjust the values. Stored only on this phone.
Used for calories, training load and fitness estimates. Stored only on this phone.
Fill in your profile in Settings to see calories and training load.
Not enough heart rate data yet.
Basal is what your body burns even sitting still, so it grows through the day. Active counts only effort recorded with the ring on: a workout without the ring is not counted.
A trend needs about two weeks of heart rate data.
Estimates from heart rate and your profile (Banister TRIMP, Keytel, Mifflin-St Jeor). Calories can be far off; the trend is not an injury predictor.
No sleep found in the last day and a half. The level needs a recorded night to start from: wear the ring tonight.
Our own model: sleep recharges, stress and effort drain. A guide to your pattern, not a measurement.
No recorded night yet. Wear the ring while you sleep.
Score, debt and bedtime are our own heuristics. Naps are guessed from a calm, low heart rate: quiet sitting can look the same.
This method agrees poorly with measured VO2max at your age: look only at the trend.
Repeated dips under your night median. The ring only stores one SpO2 value per hour, so this is a hint, not a diagnosis: if you snore or wake tired, ask a doctor.
Not enough tagged incidents yet. Tag incidents with categories (caffeine, alcohol, exercise...) and wear the ring at night: a pattern needs at least 5 nights per category.
Compares the night after each tagged incident with your other nights. Correlation, not proof.
Sit still for three minutes, hand resting, no talking. The ring records the raw pulse signal and the app looks at whether the timing between heartbeats is regular.
Pulse irregular in this check. Repeat it while sitting calmly.
Not enough clean beats. Keep your hand still and try again.
One irregular result this week: repeat the check in a few hours.
Irregular results at different times this week. This is not a diagnosis, but it is worth an ECG: talk to a doctor, and seek help right away with chest pain, breathlessness or fainting.

Screening only, never a diagnosis. Tuned on public ECG data from atrial fibrillation patients (sensitivity about 90%, specificity about 95%) and not validated on real atrial fibrillation with this ring. Extra beats and movement can look irregular, so repeat it before drawing conclusions.
Shaded stretches: no data, the ring was not worn. They are left out of the charts and of every average and estimate.

HRV (heart rate variability) is the small variation in the time between heartbeats. Higher usually means a more relaxed, recovered body; it drops with stress, illness, alcohol and poor sleep. It is measured as RMSSD, in milliseconds. Compare it only with your own usual values: people differ a lot.
The ring\'s own estimate from your HRV and heart rate: higher means your body looks more tense. It reflects your body, not your mood, and it is not a psychological test.

SpO2 is the percentage of oxygen carried by your blood. About 95-100% is normal. The ring measures it with light on the finger, so it is approximate and drifts with cold hands, movement and a loose fit.
Skin temperature at the finger, not core body temperature. It moves with the room, exercise and your cycle: the trend over several nights says more than a single reading.
Breaths per minute, estimated from the small changes in your heartbeat timing as you breathe. It needs a calm, still measurement.

Compares last night\'s HRV and resting heart rate, plus how much you slept, with your own recent norm. Higher means you look better recovered than usual. It needs a few days of data before it means anything.
Our own model of your energy reserve: sleep refills it, stress and effort drain it. Use it to compare one day with another, not as a measurement. It needs a recorded night to start from.

The score (0-100) mixes how long you slept against your target, how continuous it was and how much deep and REM sleep you got. Debt is the sleep you missed over the last 7 nights. Regularity is how consistent your sleep start is.

TRIMP is training load: minutes at a raised heart rate, weighted so that harder effort counts much more. The trend compares your last 7 days with your usual. VO2max is an indicative fitness estimate from your resting heart rate: watch the trend, not the number. Recovery is how many beats per minute your heart rate fell 5 minutes after an effort.

Checks whether the timing between your heartbeats is regular. Irregular timing can come from atrial fibrillation, but also from extra beats, movement or a poor signal, so repeat it before drawing conclusions. It is a screening, never a diagnosis.
Looks at whether the nights after things you tagged (coffee, alcohol, hard exercise...) differ from your other nights in HRV, resting heart rate and sleep. It shows a correlation, not a cause.
Estimates, from the nightly skin temperature, whether the slight rise that follows ovulation has happened. Optional and experimental; it is not a contraceptive or a fertility tool.
Needs about three weeks of nightly skin temperature (%1$d nights so far).
No sustained post-ovulation temperature rise in the recent nights.
The temperature rise that usually follows ovulation started %1$d nights ago.

Skin temperature only. Not a contraceptive and not for planning or avoiding pregnancy: illness, alcohol and a warm room can look like a rise. Feedback from people who track their cycle is very welcome.
Touch or drag on the chart to read the exact time and value.
